name: Dalosirvat (SM-04554)

card.summary: An investigational topical Wnt-pathway activator developed for androgenetic alopecia, aimed at regrowing scalp hair and thickening thinning areas.
card.note: Investigational; not approved by regulators for sale.

quick.overview:
Dalosirvat (SM-04554) is an experimental topical drug for pattern hair loss. It is designed to switch on the Wnt signalling pathway, which is involved in hair-follicle growth, so that miniaturised follicles produce thicker, longer hair.
If it works as intended, the appearance payoff would be a fuller hairline and crown. A 2021 patent review lists it among Wnt modulators in late-stage development for androgenetic alopecia.
quick.how: It has been studied as a topical product applied to the scalp, developed by the company Samumed (now Biosplice). It is not a prescription or over-the-counter product that people can obtain through a pharmacy.
quick.risks: As an investigational compound its safety profile is defined only by clinical-trial data, and it is not approved for sale. Wnt signalling also has roles in other tissues, which is why researchers study topical delivery.

lead: Dalosirvat, also called SM-04554, is a topical Wnt pathway activator being developed for androgenetic alopecia [1]. Wnt signalling is a pathway involved in embryonic development and tissue maintenance [1].

The idea is to stimulate hair follicles through Wnt signalling rather than through hormone blockade, which is how finasteride works. For people with thinning hair, the target outcome is regrowth and thicker hair.
A 2021 patent review described SM-04554 as a Wnt activator for androgenetic alopecia in Phase III development, alongside lorecivivint, a Wnt inhibitor for knee osteoarthritis [1].

chain: Topical Wnt pathway activation at the scalp
Thicker, fuller hair in thinning areas
angle.text: The compound is aimed at reversing the follicle miniaturisation behind pattern hair loss. Its intended effect is more visible hair density on the scalp.

paras: Dalosirvat has been developed for androgenetic alopecia, the common pattern hair loss in men and women [1].
SM-04554 is described as a Wnt signalling activator [1]. Wnt signalling has a vital role in embryonic development and normal tissue preservation [1].
A 2021 patent review of Wnt modulators listed SM-04554 as being in Phase III for androgenetic alopecia [1].
No peer-reviewed trial results for dalosirvat have been published; a 2021 patent review reports it as in Phase III development for androgenetic alopecia [1].

timeline.event: A patent review lists SM-04554 as a Wnt activator in Phase III for androgenetic alopecia [1].
